title: Energy Requirement Calculator
desc: RER, MER by k factor — dog, Expected water intake — dog, MER by k factor — cat, Expected water intake — cat

meds.name: RER
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'RER = 70 × kg0.75 = 70 × '+R2(kg)+'0.75 = '+R2(70*Math.pow(kg,0.75))+' kcal/day
Maintenance ER = k × RER — pick the k factor below.'

meds.name: MER by k factor — dog
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>{var r=70*Math.pow(kg,0.75);var k=[['Typical neutered pet',1.6],['Weight loss (overweight)',1.0],['Obese prone',1.4],['Weight gain (neutered)',2.0],['Weight gain (intact)',2.2]];return k.map(function(x){return x[0]+' (k='+x[1]+') → '+R2(x[1]*r)+' kcal/day';}).join('
');}

meds.name: Expected water intake — dog
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'Water intake is about 1 ml per kcal.
PU/PD threshold is over 100 ml/kg/day = '+R2(kg*100)+' ml/day = '+R2(kg*100/236.6)+' cups/day.'

meds.name: RER
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'RER = 70 × kg0.75 = '+R2(70*Math.pow(kg,0.75))+' kcal/day
Maintenance ER = k × RER — pick the k factor below.'

meds.name: MER by k factor — cat
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>{var r=70*Math.pow(kg,0.75);var k=[['Weight loss (overweight)',0.8],['Obese prone',1.0],['Weight gain (neutered)',1.47],['Weight gain (intact)',1.7],['Light / active working',1.6],['Typical intact pet',1.4],['Typical neutered pet',1.2],['Critical care',1.0],['Healthy kitten',2.5]];return k.map(function(x){return x[0]+' (k='+x[1]+') → '+R2(x[1]*r)+' kcal/day';}).join('
');}

meds.name: Expected water intake — cat
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'Water intake is about 1 ml per kcal.
PU/PD threshold is over 100 ml/kg/day = '+R2(kg*100)+' ml/day = '+R2(kg*100/236.6)+' cups/day.'

notes: See Below for Water Deprivation Testing
Lactation Calorie Requirements ( table from VIN)
Water Dep test: d/c if Na > 165 or osmolality > 350
(look-up table depends on age of pups/kittens)
Normal osmolality for dog = 280 to 310, cat = 180 to 310
Measure water intake daily 3-5 days for average
Weigh, check SpG on day 1 before water deprivation
Each AM: check weight, SpG & Na
Reduce water by 5 to 10% each day
If the patient becomes 5% dehydrated or loses 5% body weight, empty the bladder and check USG.
Administer DDAVP at 4 drops of 100 µg/mL solution either intranasally or into the conjunctival sac.
Hospitalize the patient and check USG in 3 hours.8 If USG is >1.025, the diagnosis is CDI. If USG is <1.025, NDI is the most likely diagnosis
